messages.subject: Re: Rattle with Revolution R
parts:
The specific error re paste0 is fixed in more recent versions.

You could try:

> install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com")

Regards,
Graham

On Sunday, March 17, 2013 9:17:51 PM UTC+11, davidj...@btconnect.com wrote:
Hi,
I've used Rattle successfully for a while and am an ardent fan. I am trying to use Rattle with Revolution R 5.1.0. The current version runs R 2.14.2.
I am running Win 7 Pro with all patches and updates.
 
When I install rattle, I get the following messages (which appear to be a red herring):
 
Version 2.6.25 r42 Copyright (c) 2006-2013 Togaware Pty Ltd.
Type 'rattle()' to shake, rattle, and roll your data.
> rattle()
Error in inDL(x, as.logical(local), as.logical(now), ...) :
 
unable to load shared object 'C:/Revolution/R-Enterprise-6.1/R-2.14.2/library/RGtk2/libs/x64/RGtk2.dll':
 
LoadLibrary failure:  The specified module could not be found.
 
trying URL 'http://ftp.gnome.org/pub/gnome/binaries/win64/gtk+/2.22/gtk+-bundle_2.22.1-20101229_win64.zip'
Content type 'application/zip' length 25830230 bytes (24.6 Mb)
opened URL
downloaded 24.6 Mb
 
Learn more about GTK+ at http://www.gtk.org
If the package still does not load, please ensure that GTK+ is installed and that it is on your PATH environment variable

IN ANY CASE, RESTART R BEFORE TRYING TO LOAD THE PACKAGE AGAIN
Error in configureGUI() : could not find function "paste0"
In addition: Warning messages:
1: Failed to load RGtk2 dynamic library, attempting to install it.
2: In dir.create(config_path, recursive = TRUE) :
 
'C:\Revolution\R-Enterprise-6.1\R-2.14.2\library\RGtk2\gtk\x64\etc\gtk-2.0' already exists
>
 
If I run a Rattle generated script, it happily loads and executes RGtk2 etc. and completes.
 
However when running rattle()
I get the message:
 
Error in configureGUI() : could not find function "paste0"
 
The Rattle GUI loads, but nothing happens buttons are clicked, neither do the they have any annotation.
I have done all of the usual things such as reinstalling Revolution R, checking the path etc.
 
It's most frustrating as I has hoped that I would be able to use the libraries in Revolution to speed up execution.
 
Most grateful for any help you can give.

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Rattle with Revolution R
parts:
Oops - sorry for the bad steer... only the latest version of R under Windows is supported for the beta downloads.

You could try:

> paste0 <- function(..., collapse=NULL) paste(..., collapse=collapse, sep="")

then start up Rattle.

Regards,
Graham
